request: Add several cutouts into the part to decrease its weight.

actions.operation: Create multiple cutout features (material removal cuts) in the part

parameters.proposed_pattern: linear pattern along X, symmetric about XZ mid-plane (y=0)
parameters.proposed_slot_width: to be defined (suggest start ~30–45% of local beam width at each slot location)
parameters.proposed_web_ligament_min: to be defined (keep-out to preserve strength near interfaces; suggest >= 1.5–2.0x local thickness from outer edges and >= 2.0x thickness from end-interface blend zones)
parameters.proposed_edge_fillet: to be defined (suggest small fillet on cutout edges for stress relief, e.g., R0.5–R2 depending on scale)

actions.target: the part (solid body), primarily the Tapered Beam / Main Web region to reduce mass while preserving both end interfaces
actions.relational_constraint: Cutouts should be placed in Section S2 (tapered beam) and must not break into or weaken critical functional interfaces: (a) clevis pin bores and lug walls in Section S1, (b) hook/notch seat cylinders and end post region in Section S3. Maintain symmetry about the XZ mid-plane (y=0) and keep sufficient ligaments to outer side planes and top/bottom planes for stiffness and fatigue resistance. Prefer rounded/obround cutouts with filleted edges to reduce stress concentrations.
actions.unresolved_reference: Exact number of cutouts; exact cutout dimensions (length/width/end radii); exact placement along X; exact minimum ligament/keep-out distances relative to S1 pin hole centerlines and S3 notch/post; whether cutouts must be identical or vary with taper; manufacturing constraints (milling vs casting/printing) that set minimum radii and wall thickness; whether cutouts should be through-all or blind pockets. Multiview images show a tapered solid web with no existing lightening features, but do not provide explicit dimensions for robust sizing.
steps: Identify keep-out regions to preserve functional behavior: exclude Section S1 clevis end (pin interfaces FACE 0/0000 and FACE 1/0001, slot end wall FACE 2/0002, and surrounding lug material) and exclude Section S3 hook end (notch/seat cylinders FACE 7/0007 and FACE 8/0008, outer hook cylinder FACE 10/0010, post cylinder FACE 13/0013 and post cap FACE 17/0017). Define an allowable lightening window within Section S2 bounded by a conservative offset from the S1-to-S2 blend and S2-to-S3 blend (offset distances to be defined).

Start a new sketch on the Top major plane of the tapered beam: select FACE 5 (face_code 0005) as the sketch plane. Use the part origin reference and/or create a construction centerline along the part longitudinal axis (X direction) on this sketch.

Project/convert key outer edges of Section S2 into the sketch (top silhouette edges and/or references to side planes FACE 16/0016 and FACE 9/0009) to understand the local available width at each prospective cutout location and to constrain cutouts away from the outer boundaries.

Create the first obround (slot) profile centered on the mid-plane y=0: draw a center-point slot (or two tangent arcs + two lines) with its long axis aligned to X. Constrain the slot centerline coincident with y=0 (symmetry plane) so the cutout is centered laterally. Dimension the slot width and end radius (end radius = 0.5*width recommended as a starting point) and dimension slot length to fit within the local taper while maintaining the minimum ligament to the outer boundaries (to be defined).

Create additional obround slot profiles (for 'several' cutouts) within the allowable lightening window: add two more slots along the same centerline (y=0), spaced along X. Constrain slot-to-slot spacing equal (linear pattern) or dimension each slot position as a percentage of the Section S2 length (e.g., 25%, 50%, 75% of the usable S2 span), ensuring all remain clear of S1 and S3 keep-out zones and do not approach the transition blends where stress is highest.

Apply sketch constraints for robustness: keep each slot fully inside the projected Section S2 outline by applying offset constraints from the projected outer edges (maintain the minimum ligament), and keep slots aligned with the X axis via parallel constraints to the projected longitudinal edges. Ensure the sketch is fully constrained.

Perform an Extrude-Cut from the top face: cut the three slot profiles 'Through All' (or 'Up to Face' targeting the Bottom major plane FACE 11 / face_code 0011) normal to the sketch plane so each cutout fully removes material through the thickness of the tapered beam without leaving thin caps.

Stress-relief the cutout boundaries: apply edge fillets to the newly created cutout edges on both top and bottom openings (fillet radius to be defined; choose the largest radius allowed by minimum ligament and manufacturing process). This reduces stress concentration and improves fatigue performance while achieving weight reduction intent.

Validate interface protection and strength intent: confirm that the through-cuts do not intersect Section S1 critical faces (pin bores face_code 0000/0001 and clevis walls) and do not intersect Section S3 notch/post faces (face_code 0007/0008/0013/0017). Check remaining wall thickness/ligaments to side planes (face_code 0016 and 0009) and to top/bottom planes (face_code 0005 and 0011) across the taper; adjust slot widths/lengths accordingly to preserve stiffness near the ends and achieve weight reduction primarily in the mid-span.

intention: Decrease the part's weight (reduce mass) while preserving the functional interfaces at the clevis/pin end (Section S1) and the hook/notch/post end (Section S3), and maintaining adequate strength/fatigue performance by placing rounded lightening cutouts in the tapered main web (Section S2).
